propositions: User identity differs between Cloud (opaque accountId) and Data Center (name), requiring a polymorphic contract to avoid leaking deployment-specific logic into outbound mapping.

PR #120's DC implementation consulted an unset _assignee_resolver attribute, making the authoritative branch unreachable and causing permanent non-authoritative assignee resolution that triggers outbound diff churn.

A UserIdentityModel protocol with resolve() and to_payload() methods allows AccountIdIdentity (Cloud) and NameIdentity (DC) to encapsulate deployment-specific identity handling and resolver injection as explicit parameters.

NameIdentity must perform a real lookup against DC's user-search endpoint to return authoritative=True for resolvable assignees, ending the churn cycle that occurs when assignee resolution always returns authoritative=False.
The contract test must verify the three-state resolution outcome (converged/authoritative, non-authoritative, unresolvable error) holds identically across both implementations.
